summary: Six come fast (US, Japan, Canada, England, Australia, Scotland), Germany, France, South Korea and Sweden take thought, and China, Spain, Ireland and South Africa sit just below at #11 to #14.
reasons: Casual found 7 before running out (US, Scotland, England via 'uk', Japan, Canada, Australia, Germany); lives went on Ireland #13, China #11, Spain #12, South Africa #14 and Mexico (outside the top 20). A weaker order found 6. Fan found all 10, losing lives on Ireland, South Africa and Spain.

Every answer is a country anyone knows, and the order is reasoned from wealth, space and golf culture. Japan at 3,169 and the US at 43% of all courses are good reveals; Sweden and South Korea are the fair stretches.

Fairness 3: four golf-famous countries sit at #11 to #14, all within 125 courses of Scotland, so lives go fast. Each shows its figure, and countries below the count read 'outside the top 20', so the misses teach something.

Data matches the Golf course article's 2019 R&A table and the prompt states the year and the England/Scotland split. 'uk', 'britain' and 'gb' offer both; 'golf', Wales, Northern Ireland, St Andrews and Augusta are free; 'korea' and 'holland' resolve.
Judge's note: the builder's placeholder named most answers before the prediction step, so the fan's order was set by golf culture, not recall of the table. Treat the replays as slightly generous.
fixes: scripts/facts/golf-countries.json, Canada: 'the oldest golf club in North America still in existence' contradicts its own evidence (The Savannah Golf Club, 1794, still exists). Say 'the oldest in North America in continuous existence'.
